{"id": "bcb10947-fcdf-4293-8a05-02008c282a24", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What is the difference between an Application Load Balancer and a Network Load Balancer?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "cfd89b8a-3e97-4937-b0e4-f9043d68088b", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is general AWS knowledge about ALB vs NLB, not specific to the DevOps Agent product, so I can answer directly without needing to verify against product documentation.\n\n"}]}

{"id": "0d36b378-aaa7-45d1-8038-bafb60328f3c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The main difference is the network layer each one works at. An ALB works at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS). An NLB works at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS).

| | **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** | **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query strings, HTTP methods, source IP | Flow-based: protocol and port, using a 5-tuple hash |
| **Performance** | Good, but it inspects each request, so it adds more latency | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency, and it handles sudden traffic spikes well |
| **IP addresses** | DNS name only, and the IPs can change | One static IP per Availability Zone, and you can attach Elastic IPs |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, and ALBs |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS with SNI and can authenticate users through OIDC or Cognito | Can terminate TLS or pass it through unchanged, which is useful for end-to-end encryption |
| **Source IP** | The client IP arrives in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserves the client source IP, depending on target type |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023), but the NLB must be created with them |
| **Extras** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, WAF integration | PrivateLink (endpoint services) support, and it can forward non-HTTP protocols |

**Choose an ALB when you:**
- Run web apps, REST APIs, or microservices and want path- or host-based routing, for example `/api` to one service and `/web` to another.
- Need AWS WAF, authentication at the load balancer, or HTTP-level redirects.
- Want to route to Lambda functions.

**Choose an NLB when you:**
- Need extreme performance, millions of requests per second, or very low latency.
- Handle non-HTTP traffic such as gaming, IoT, MQTT, DNS, or custom TCP/UDP protocols.
- Need static or Elastic IPs, for example when clients allowlist your IPs.
- Want to expose a service privately through AWS PrivateLink.

You can also put an NLB in front of an ALB. That gives you static IPs and PrivateLink while keeping Layer 7 routing behind it.
